title: DXF view-family code-context correction: HEADER VisualStyle pointers versus VIEWPORT
scope: class-specific meaning of DXF group codes 334, 345, 346, and 349
HEADER VisualStyle hard-pointer variables and rooted reference closure
local DXF and DWG header parser/writer preservation gaps
PAR-40 / 7G.2 implementation ordering and version gates

sources.finding: HEADER defines $INTERFEREOBJVS at code 345 and $INTERFEREVPVS at code 346 as VisualStyle hard pointers, and $DRAGVS at code 349 as a VisualStyle hard pointer; documented defaults are Conceptual, 3D Wireframe, and null respectively.
VIEWPORT assigns 345/346 to named/base UCS, uses 333 for shade target and 348 for VisualStyle, and does not list code 349.
VIEW assigns code 334 to its optional LiveSection soft-pointer reference; this does not establish a VIEWPORT code-334 field.
The 340-349 range is a generic hard-pointer range; the range does not define class-specific carrier semantics.

The Rust dxf crate models $DRAGVS as a solid-visual-style handle and reports AutoCAD R2007 as the minimum version. This is secondary corroboration for $DRAGVS only, not a normative gate for all three HEADER pointers.

confirmed_gaps: DRW_Viewport::parseCode assigns undocumented VIEWPORT code 349 into shadePlotHandle; writeViewport emits that value as code 333, conflating fields.
DRW_Header::parseCode has no 345/346/349 cases and drops the three HEADER pointer values.
The R2007+ DWG header parser reads the three corresponding handles into temporary CONTROL values used only for debug output.
The DWG header encoder writes null hard pointers for the three values.
context_corrections: Do not add DRW_Viewport::dragVisualStyleHandle; code 349 belongs to HEADER $DRAGVS in the verified DXF reference.
Do not add a VIEWPORT code-334 field; code 334 is documented on VIEW as LiveSection.
Code 345/346 meanings are carrier-specific: HEADER VisualStyle pointers differ from VIEWPORT named/base UCS references.
unresolved_contracts: Exact first supported release, source-version behavior, and null/absent defaults for each HEADER variable independently.
Exact ODA DWG header-variable handle layout, ordering, null encoding, and version gates for AC1021 and later.
Required destination-preserving behavior when a HEADER target is missing, ambiguous, wrong-class, or unrooted.

corrected_sequence: Stop the VIEWPORT code-349 to code-333 alias without adding a viewport field.
Implement the three HEADER VisualStyle hard-pointer routes only after their independent version/default/root contracts are established.
Before changing DWG parsing or encoding, read the repository-mandated ODA specification and trace version-matched samples.
Test generated ASCII/Binary handle remaps, null/absence, graph negatives, destination preservation, and adapter retry; do not add external fixture files.
